subtitulo: Order the base, then use with, without, on the side, less spicy, more and no ice
cena: Two identical orders just left the same window built completely differently, and the only thing that changed was six small words.
frasePiso: You can turn one menu choice into the taco and drink you actually want without explaining your diet.

clique.desconto: Nobody handed you six separate rules for customising an order. You built all six out of two small words — con and sin — plus three targeted follow-ups.
clique.piso: Next time a menu doesn't have exactly what you want, you won't order the closest thing and hope. You'll ask for the base and shape it yourself.

steps.pt: The menu gives you the base — six small controls change the result. Start with quantity and the item as listed.

steps.es: Quería dos tacos al pastor, por favor.
steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah dohs TAH-kohs al pahs-TOR por fah-BOR
steps.pt: I'd like two tacos al pastor, please.
steps.tts: Quería dos tacos al pastor, por favor.

steps.promptPt: At the cashier from B11, order two of the rotating-spit tacos named on the menu. Speak now.
steps.es: Quería dos tacos al pastor, por favor.
steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah dohs TAH-kohs al pahs-TOR por fah-BOR
steps.pt: I'd like two tacos al pastor, please.
With everything?
Todo isn't a fixed list — answer with what you actually want. Con adds the ingredients you name.

steps.promptPt: For the first taco, accept the chopped onion and cilantro offered at this counter. Speak now.
steps.pt: One with onion and cilantro.
Very good.
Second taco, different build. The frame is sin plus an ingredient — not an allergy guarantee, B13 covers that.

steps.promptPt: Your companion wants the second taco without the chopped onion. Change only that taco. Speak now.
steps.es: El otro sin cebolla, por favor.
steps.pinyin: el OH-troh seen seh-BOH-yah por fah-BOR
steps.pt: The other one without onion, please.
Of course.
Keep the salsa reversible — aparte puts it beside the taco, so you control the first taste yourself.

steps.promptPt: Ask for the salsa in a separate small container, not poured over either taco. Speak now.
steps.pt: The salsa on the side, please.
Yes, here you are.
Colour doesn't reliably signal heat — ask which one's milder and follow the gesture to this batch.

steps.promptPt: Two unlabelled salsas are beside the tacos. Ask which one is less spicy. Speak now.
steps.pt: Which salsa is less spicy?
This one is less spicy.
Más asks for one visible extra, not a bigger portion overall — name the thing, like the lime.

steps.promptPt: The tray has one lime wedge for two tacos. Ask for more lime. Speak now.
steps.pt: More lime, please.
Of course, here you are.
The same sin frame works on drinks — name it, remove the ice. Preference, not a health claim.

steps.promptPt: Add one lemonade but ask for it without ice. Speak now.
steps.es: Una limonada sin hielo, por favor.
steps.pinyin: OO-nah lee-moh-NAH-dah seen YEH-loh por fah-BOR
steps.pt: One lemonade without ice, please.
Very good.

steps.promptPt: A complete sentence with no verb. Speak now.
steps.pt: Without chilli, please.

steps.promptPt: Only your plate changes, not your companion’s. Speak now.
steps.pt: Mine without cream.

steps.promptPt: This one is too hot. Ask for a different one. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I have a different salsa?

steps.es: Uno con cebolla y cilantro. El otro sin cebolla. La salsa aparte. Más limón. Una limonada sin hielo.
steps.pinyin: OO-noh kohn seh-BOH-yah ee see-LAHN-troh. el OH-troh seen seh-BOH-yah. lah SAHL-sah ah-PAHR-teh. mahs lee-MOHN. OO-nah lee-moh-NAH-dah seen YEH-loh
steps.pt: Shadow the five controls after the base order.
steps.tts: Uno con cebolla y cilantro. El otro sin cebolla. La salsa aparte. Más limón. Una limonada sin hielo.

steps.pt: B12 complete. Base order, con adds, sin removes, aparte keeps salsa reversible, más adds — allergy gets its own route next.

secoes.titulo: Con todo is a question, not a fixed recipe
secoes.corpo: When you hear ¿Con todo?, do not assume a national list. Answer with the ingredients you want in the scene: con cebolla y cilantro, or remove a named preference with sin.

secoes.titulo: Aparte makes the first taste reversible
secoes.corpo: Salsa aparte keeps the sauce beside the taco. You can test a small amount after asking which current batch pica menos.
Salsa colour reflects ingredients and preparation. Ask ¿Cuál salsa pica menos? and use the answer for the batch in front of you; do not turn green and red into a permanent rule.
Sin cebolla and sin hielo customise an order. They do not communicate allergy severity, cross-contact or kitchen procedure. B13 deliberately changes both the language and the artifact.

permissao: You are allowed to build two completely different orders from the same base without explaining why. Con and sin need no justification — a taquería absorbs custom orders constantly, and asking which salsa is milder is a normal question, not a fussy one.
espelho: Ordering a coffee 'with oat milk, no foam, extra hot' back home is the exact same move as con cebolla y cilantro, sin hielo here — nobody thinks twice about customising a drink at a familiar counter, and a taco counter runs on the same con/sin logic once you have the two words.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You pick the red salsa because you remember reading that red is usually milder than green, and it turns out to be the spicier of the two on the counter.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I misremembered the rule, or salsas here don't follow logic.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Salsa colour in Mexico reflects the specific ingredients and preparation of that batch, not a fixed heat scale — a red salsa made with dried chiles can easily outrank a mild green tomatillo salsa, and the reverse is just as common.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Ask ¿cuál salsa pica menos? and let the answer be about the two salsas actually in front of you, not a colour rule from somewhere else.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You get an answer calibrated to this counter's actual batch instead of a memorised rule that fails as often as it works.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a reason to distrust every food colour cue in Mexican cuisine — this is specifically about salsa heat, where colour genuinely doesn't predict intensity.
